side-to-side-blend.motion: Start with the Sky blue at the top and stroke side to side. Without rinsing, pick up the Sunset gold and paint below it, down past the hill line. Then stroke back up over the join several times.
side-to-side-blend.result: Smooth bands of sky, blue at the top and gold above the hills, with a soft join where the two wet colors meet.
side-to-side-blend.then: Stroke back over the blue-gold join while it's wet.

mistakes.mistake: A hard line where the blue meets the gold.
mistakes.fix: Add more Sunset gold at the join and blend again.

mistakes.mistake: The blue and the gold won't blend; the join turns greenish.
mistakes.fix: Mix a bridge color from a little of each on the palette and paint it between them.
Wipe it on a rag. Rinse before going into the gold.

diagram.title: Blend the sky blue into the gold

dry-brush.motion: Light pressure, skimming the dry sky in long sideways streaks.
dry-brush.result: Feathery, broken, see-through cloud streaks that catch the canvas texture, with the blue showing through. Never a solid area.
dry-brush.then: Build the streaks up in several light passes.

mistakes.mistake: The clouds went on as solid gray bars.
mistakes.fix: Let it dry, then dry-brush the sky blue back over part of them.

diagram.title: Skim the streaks with almost no paint

horizontal-strokes.motion: Keep the brush level and the strokes long, left and right along each range of hills.
horizontal-strokes.result: Flat, level bands of blue hills that seem to stretch away, with slight streaks that follow the stroke.
horizontal-strokes.then: Keep the back range lighter and smoother than the front one.

diagram.title: Long and level across the hills

curved-strokes.motion: Bend every stroke with the loch's shore: a long, nearly level curve from the hills' edge out to the right edge of the canvas.
curved-strokes.result: Marks that bend with the shore, which is what makes the water look like it lies flat between the hills.
curved-strokes.then: Use the Pale silver-gray for the body of the water and the Pale gold shine along its top edge, both following the curve.

stages.caption: Curved strokes, gold along the top

flicking.motion: A quick stroke upward from the bottom of each blade, lifting off as it goes, so each blade thins at the top.
flicking.result: Tapered grass blades with broken tips, denser at the base.
flicking.then: Flick the Olive gold over the moss green next step, fewer as you go up, so the dark green shows between the blades.

diagram.title: Flick each blade up from its base

stages.caption: Fewer olive gold ones on top

build-from-pieces.motion: Start with one simple shape: a big oval for the cow's body. Then add the head on its upper right and the fringe on top in curved pieces, smaller toward the edges.
build-from-pieces.result: A cow shape made of distinct curved pieces, body, head, and fringe, with small gaps or overlaps between them.
build-from-pieces.then: Soften where the pieces meet only where the hair should look smooth; otherwise leave the pieces showing.

thick-to-thin.motion: Press the full width of the brush where the lock starts, then turn onto its edge or tip and lighten the pressure as the lock hangs down. With an angle brush, the lighter you press, the thinner the lock.
thick-to-thin.result: A lock of hair that starts wide and tapers to a point.
thick-to-thin.then: Add a few thinner wisps with a liner.
